To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the problem of private convex optimization can be reduced to the problem of private localization; (ii) the problem of localization can be solved using the privacy amplifying effect of iterative algorithms; (iii) the privacy amplification technique is applicable to a broad class of optimization algorithms.

(1) The optimal rate for private stochastic convex optimization can be attained in linear time, (2) The optimal rate can be attained for strongly convex objectives in linear time, and (3) The optimal rate of convergence can be attained for non smooth objectives in sublinear time
(i) the optimal excess population loss can be achieved in linear time and (ii) this is the only regime where this holds.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether private stochastic convex optimization algorithms can achieve the same efficiency as non-private algorithms, and we show that this is indeed the case.
the design of private stochastic convex optimization: Optimal rates in linear time.
the design and analysis of private stochastic convex optimization algorithms with optimal excess population loss guarantees.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown that there exist differentially private stochastic convex optimization algorithms that are both optimal in terms of the excess population loss, and efficient in terms of the running time.
we have a linear time algorithm with optimal excess loss for the smooth case and optimal excess loss with a sublinear running time for the non-smooth case.
we give a complete and optimal picture for DP stochastic convex optimization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide optimal algorithms for the stochastic convex optimization problem that run in the same time as their non private counterparts.
for any smooth and convex loss function, we give a differentially private algorithm with excess loss of order O(1/n), using O(n) gradient computations.
we provide the first linear time algorithms for differentially private convex optimization with optimal excess population loss.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the privacy amplification technique can be used to derive efficient algorithms in a wider variety of settings.
, in contrast with the non private case, the problem of designing efficient DP stochastic convex optimization algorithms is far from being solved.

, in the stochastic convex optimization setting, the optimal excess loss bound can be achieved using algorithms with running time that is essentially the same as the running time of optimal non private algorithms.
